publicTrace: Base rate: Annual average CPI-U changes for 2020-2024 were +1.2%, +4.7%, +8.0%, +4.1%, +2.9%, showing a clear post-pandemic deceleration trend toward the 2-3% range.

Mechanism: The 2026 annual average is computed as (avg of all 12 monthly 2026 CPI-U values) / (avg of all 12 monthly 2025 CPI-U values) - 1. With 5 months of 2026 data averaging 330.08 and 11 months of 2025 data averaging 321.94, the YTD 2026-vs-observed-2025 gap is +2.53%. The carry-forward statistic of ~3.44% reflects the mechanical effect of already-observed 2026 levels relative to a full 2025 average that still needs one more month (December 2025 is missing from the API).

Point estimate rationale: Assuming the remaining 7 months of 2026 (Jun-Dec) print near the recent monthly pace (~0.2-0.3% MoM), and December 2025 fills in near the observed 2025 trend, the full-year 2026 vs full-year 2025 annual average change is estimated at approximately 2.8%, consistent with gradual disinflation continuing but tariff and services-sector pressures keeping inflation above the Fed's 2% target on an annual-average basis.

Disconfirming consideration (upside): The recentAnnualizedPct of ~10.6% signals that the most recent monthly prints (Apr-May 2026) were unusually high, possibly reflecting tariff pass-through. If this pace persists, the annual average change could exceed 4-5%, pushing the outcome well above the central estimate and outside the 80% interval.

Disconfirming consideration (downside): A sharp demand slowdown, energy price collapse, or rapid tariff reversal could bring monthly prints near zero or negative for the remainder of 2026, potentially pulling the annual average change below 2%, outside the lower bound of the 80% interval.

Data caveat: December 2025 is missing from the BLS API response (only 11 months observed), so the 2025 annual average denominator is incomplete; the final 2026-vs-2025 percent change will depend on the December 2025 print, adding meaningful uncertainty to the denominator.
assumptions: December 2025 CPI-U will print near the trend of the other 2025 months (~321-323 range), completing the 2025 annual average close to the current 11-month observed average of 321.94.
Monthly CPI-U prints for June-December 2026 will average approximately 0.2-0.3% MoM, consistent with a gradual disinflation path, rather than sustaining the elevated recent annualized pace of ~10.6%.
No major structural breaks (e.g., severe recession, energy shock, or dramatic tariff reversal) occur in H2 2026 that would shift the trajectory by more than 1 percentage point from the central path.
dataCaveats: The 2025 annual average is based on only 11 months of BLS data; December 2025 is missing, making the denominator for the 2026-vs-2025 change uncertain.
The recentAnnualizedPct of ~10.6% is based on the most recent short-window monthly data and may reflect transitory factors (e.g., tariff front-loading) rather than a sustained trend.
The carry-forward annual average inflation of ~3.44% is a mechanical projection assuming 2026 monthly levels remain flat at the May 2026 level; actual outcomes will differ as new months are added.
BLS may revise monthly CPI-U values, which could alter both the 2025 and 2026 annual averages after initial publication.
drivers: Tariff pass-through to consumer prices in 2026
